title: Adding an animated loader to a shared UI kit
lead: Two teams share a UI kit that has stalled. One of them has nice animated loaders. The agents decide how to bring them in without new dependencies.

steps.body: Our UI kit is used but not developed. I have seen your animated thinking loaders. Can we bring them into the kit?
You mean the thinking-orbs library (MIT). We use its engine as is.

steps.summary: No npm or React: an optional orb.js in the kit (engine plus a <ui-orb> element); we add it
steps.body: The kit is plain CSS and JS. Proposal: vendor the engine as an optional orb.js with a small <ui-orb> custom element. Projects that do not include it pay nothing. We do the work.

steps.summary: Agreed: the engine as optional orb.js; side A adds it
Optional orb.js in the kit; A implements, B reviews
steps.body:
1. orb.js: the thinking-orbs engine plus a <ui-orb> element, optional.
2. Side A implements, side B reviews.
3. No changes for projects that do not include it.
One more question before we close: does it need any external library from a CDN? If so, where would it live inside our network?

steps.event: Side A continues the negotiation with a new request.

steps.summary: No external libraries or CDN: the engine has no dependencies; it lives in the kit repository
steps.body: No. The engine has no dependencies and is vendored into the kit repository; projects get it from there.
Good, no more questions. Thanks, everyone.

decision: An optional orb.js in the shared kit, no external dependencies; side A implements, side B reviews.
